s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive purpura and ecchymoses with systemic involvement
salient_findings: Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura
Anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment
Amorphous eosinophilic deposits on hematoxylin-eosin staining
Positive Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence
key_facts: 1-year history of purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, and weight loss
Periorbital purpura and ecchymoses progressed over 12 months
Alcohol abuse and cognitive impairment in medical history
Elder abuse excluded
Waxy yellow papules and plaques in periocular, neck, axillary, trunk, and inguinal regions
Anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria
Normal serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results
Unremarkable radiological studies
4-mm punch biopsy showed upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits
Congo red staining was positive
Polarizing light microscopy demonstrated pale apple-green birefringence

shortlist.label: Systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of purpura, ecchymoses, and systemic involvement, along with positive Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence on biopsy

shortlist.label: Primary systemic (AL) amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment, which are common in AL amyloidosis

shortlist.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to AL amyloidosis, and the absence of monoclonal gammopathy does not rule out this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Aging-associated systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and presence of systemic symptoms, although less likely given the specific biopsy findings

shortlist.label: Wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Less common, but possible given the patient's age and systemic involvement, although biopsy findings are more suggestive of AL amyloidosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, weight loss, and the presence of waxy yellow papules and plaques, along with the biopsy findings of upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits, positive Congo red staining, and pale apple-green birefringence under polarizing light microscopy, are consistent with systemic amyloidosis. The normal SPEP and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results help to rule out primary systemic (AL) amyloidosis, which is often associated with an underlying plasma cell dyscrasia.

rejected.label: Primary systemic (AL) amyloidosis
rejected.why: Normal SPEP and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results

rejected.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
rejected.why: No evidence of plasma cell dyscrasia or abnormal light chain production

rejected.label: Aging-associated systemic amyloidosis
rejected.why: Patient's symptoms and biopsy findings are not specific to aging-associated systemic amyloidosis

rejected.label: Wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis
rejected.why: No specific evidence of transthyretin amyloidosis, such as carpal tunnel syndrome or biceps tendon rupture
